outcome: Accuracy of mWHO and CARPREG risk scores in predicting obstetric and neonatal complications
cohort: 174 pregnant women with heart disease, the majority of whom had corrective surgery and delivered between January 2007 and March 2012
finding: Nearly 50% of pregnancies in women with heart disease were associated with adverse obstetric outcomes, particularly intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR), and the mWHO risk score was better at predicting complications than the CARPREG score.
mod_finding: Maternal heart disease was predictive of mode of delivery (Thierry's spatula).
